sum: Raiffeisen Bank International reported stronger core earnings for the first nine months of 2026 and completed its acquisition of Garanti BBVA Group Romania. The Austrian lender published the figures and outlook on Tuesday, November 3, in an official release.

RBI stock traded at 63.10 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:38 CET on Friday, November 13. The quote is the latest available indication for the stock and is not presented as a comparison with a Xetra closing price.

RBI generated consolidated profit of 1,127 million euros in its core group excluding Russia from January through September. The result was 10 percent above the comparable period of 2025. Main revenues increased 8 percent year over year to 4,971 million euros.

Net interest income rose 7 percent to 3,347 million euros, while net fee and commission income increased 10 percent to 1,624 million euros. Customer loans in the core group grew 8 percent from the end of 2025 to 109 billion euros.

The earnings release also showed a 1.5 percent non-performing exposure ratio at the end of September. The provisioning ratio stood at 19 basis points for the first nine months, while the common equity tier 1 ratio excluding Russia was 15.4 percent. RBI said the capital figure assumes a worst-case scenario in which it must deconsolidate Raiffeisenbank Russia and lose its entire equity in the subsidiary.

Chief Executive Michael Höllerer said the core business was performing well and that the bank had made progress on the Garanti BBVA Romania acquisition and the planned takeover of Addiko Bank. Chief Financial Officer Kamila Makhmudova said the capital base provided flexibility for further growth.

RBI completed the acquisition of Garanti BBVA Group Romania at the beginning of November. The transaction includes Garanti Bank Romania and leasing company Motoractive IFN. RBI expects the enlarged Romanian business to become the country's third-largest bank by total assets and to serve about 2.6 million customers.

sum: Raiffeisen Bank International reported a stronger core performance for the first nine months of 2026, while keeping its full-year targets in place. In a November 3 release, the Austrian lender said consolidated profit excluding Russia rose 10 percent from the same period of 2025 to 1.127 billion euros.

Main revenues increased 8 percent to 4.971 billion euros. Net interest income advanced 7 percent to 3.347 billion euros, while net fee and commission income climbed 10 percent to 1.624 billion euros. Customer loans in the core group rose 8 percent from the end of 2025 to 109 billion euros.

RBI completed the acquisition of Garanti BBVA Group Romania at the beginning of November. The transaction includes Garanti Bank Romania and leasing company Motoractive IFN. RBI said the businesses are expected to be integrated into its existing Romanian bank in the second half of 2027.

The group also reported progress on its planned takeover of Addiko Bank. As of November 2, declarations of acceptance covered 94.84 percent of Addiko shares. RBI's 2026 guidance assumes the required approvals and settlement of the transaction in the fourth quarter, with that acceptance rate.

RBI's outlook covers the group excluding Russia and includes Garanti. Net interest income is expected to exceed 4.5 billion euros, while net fee and commission income is expected at about 2.2 billion euros. General administrative expenses are projected at about 3.9 billion euros, implying a cost-to-income ratio of about 55 percent.

The bank expects a provisioning ratio of up to 35 basis points, a consolidated return on equity of about 13 percent and customer-loan growth of about 9 percent excluding acquisitions. The return target includes a one-off positive effect of about 310 basis points linked to the assumed Addiko settlement. RBI also expects a year-end CET1 ratio of about 14.5 percent under its stated Russia deconsolidation scenario.

Management said the core business was performing well and pointed to the acquisition of Garanti BBVA Romania and the planned Addiko takeover as key initiatives. The expansion offers additional regional scale, but integration work and the conditions attached to Addiko remain important execution factors for investors.

sum: On Thursday, October 29, 2026, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria reported record net attributable profit of EUR 9.07 billion for the first nine months of the year. According to the BBVA earnings release, profit increased 13.6 percent year over year in current euros, while earnings per share rose 17.5 percent after share buybacks.

Customer lending increased 20.4 percent year over year in constant euros at the end of September. Lending rose 7.3 percent in Spain and 12 percent in Mexico, BBVA's two main markets, while net interest income increased 17.8 percent to EUR 23.24 billion.

Mexico generated EUR 4.52 billion of net attributable profit, up 8.4 percent year over year. Spain contributed EUR 3.11 billion, while South America generated EUR 821 million. The bank said recurring revenue from net interest income and fees reached EUR 30.15 billion, an increase of 17 percent.

BBVA's CET1 ratio stood at 12.21 percent at the end of September, above its target range of 11.5 to 12 percent. The bank paid a gross interim dividend of EUR 0.37 per share on October 15 and has started the second EUR 1 billion tranche of a EUR 2 billion extraordinary buyback program.

For investors, the results combine strong loan expansion with continued capital distribution. The reported cost of risk was 1.44 percent and the non-performing-loan ratio was 2.6 percent, keeping credit quality in focus as lending expands.

BBVA is a global financial group focused on retail and commercial banking, corporate and investment banking, payments, asset management and digital services. Its main franchises are in Spain, Mexico, Türkiye and South America, with specialized corporate services in the United States and Asia. In Spain and Mexico, it competes with Banco Santander and CaixaBank, while its corporate and investment-banking ambitions remain smaller in scale and product breadth than global banks such as JPMorgan Chase. The bank is using its geographic network and digital platform to deepen cross-border business, particularly between Mexico, South America, Europe and the United States.

BBVA puts AI agents’ controls to the test
sum: The bank’s new framework promises faster agent deployment and shorter software release cycles, making continuous evaluation, human oversight and operational resilience central to the next phase of its AI expansion.

BBVA is moving from individual artificial intelligence use cases towards a common framework for deploying agents across its business, setting out plans that put software assurance and operational controls at the centre of its expansion.
Unveiled on 6 October at a Strategic Talk with analysts and investors, the framework, called The Frame, is intended to standardise how the bank creates, deploys, manages and governs AI agents.
The announcement comes ahead of planned rollouts in 2027 across customer-facing services, relationship management and other banking functions.

For software testing and quality assurance teams, the significant development is the bank’s stated intention to combine faster deployment with defined agent permissions, operational boundaries and continuous performance evaluation.

As agents gain access to banking systems and take on more tasks, assurance will need to address both the quality of their outputs and the actions they are permitted to execute, according to Antonio Bravo, BBVA’s global head of AI transformation.
“‘The Frame’ will allow us to build many more agents, faster, in a way that is secure, repeatable and manageable, while maintaining control and creating value,” explained Bravo.

European stock market open: Stocks kick start November trading more cautiously
sum: - European stocks are looking more tentative to start the new week/month, although Spanish equities are enjoying some respite

European stocks are off to a rather subdued start to the new month, with most major indices observing light changes as the session gets underway. The cautious mood comes after a rough end to October as investors continue to grapple with concerns surrounding AI spending and the outlook for major central banks amid growing inflation pressures. Here are the opening changes:

After a miserable run last week, the IBEX is seen bouncing back a little and seeking a bit of a respite today. Spanish stocks had been battered by the fallout from Brazil's election shock, with banking heavyweights such as Santander and BBVA coming under significant selling pressure. The early gains today offer some welcome relief, although there's still plenty of ground to make up after the recent declines.
Besides that, there's not much appetite elsewhere across Europe. As things stand, investors are still trying to find their footing after last week's selloff in techn shares especially.

Even with the better mood in US futures today, we're not seeing that translate to any rebound in the broader risk mood. S&P 500 futures are up 0.3% with Nasdaq futures up 0.7% as tech shares lead the bounce for now. But again, it comes after a bloodbath on Friday as there remains plenty of questions surrounding lofty AI spending commitments and whether they will eventually translate into meaningful returns. And those won't be going away any time soon.

We'll still have a couple of big central bank decisions to deal with this week, with the RBA and BOE lined up. And on the economic data front, we will have Eurozone inflation data and the US jobs report on the cards too. But before we get to much of those items on the agenda, the US midterm elections tomorrow will be the bigger focus.
So, all of that should give traders plenty to chew on as November gets underway.

Garanti BBVA stock secures EUR 400 million in DPR financing
sum: Garanti BBVA has secured EUR 400 million in diversified payment rights financing, according to a BBVA announcement published on October 27, 2026. The transaction was arranged in international markets under the bank's foreign borrowing program and has maturities of 1,907 and 2,547 days.

The financing is structured through the bank's Diversified Payment Rights, or DPR, program. The structure is based on existing and future foreign-currency payment orders and is intended to diversify Garanti BBVA's wholesale funding sources while strengthening access to longer-term financing.

BBVA described the transaction as Garanti BBVA's first DPR financing since 2019. The bank's CEO Mahmut Akten said the transaction would diversify funding sources and strengthen international partnerships. Those statements describe management's strategic view and do not by themselves establish an effect on earnings or the share price.

Of the financing, EUR 50 million is designated for small and medium-sized businesses owned or managed by women. A further EUR 50 million is intended for micro, small and medium-sized businesses owned or managed by entrepreneurs under 35. BBVA said the programs are designed to support investment, growth and access to finance.

Garanti BBVA's investor-relations calendar lists the bank's third-quarter 2026 financial results webcast for November 2, 2026. That upcoming event may provide investors with additional information on funding, asset quality and the operating environment, but those details are not part of the financing announcement.

items.t: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria SA Stock (BBVA) Moved Down by 3.31% on Oct 7: What Signal Does It Send?
sum: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria SA (BBVA) moved down by 3.31%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is down by 2.01%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Bank of America Corp (BAC) down 1.45%; Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) down 2.53%; JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) down 1.20%.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria experienced downward momentum primarily driven by heightened market anxiety surrounding the crucial deadline for its tender offer to acquire Banco Sabadell. Investors are weighing the potential implications of capital deployment, shareholder acceptance thresholds, and execution risks associated with the transaction. This pending corporate action has created short-term overhang on the equity, leading institutional investors to de-risk ahead of the offer outcome.

Beyond the M&A dynamics, sentiment is impacted by macroeconomic headwinds and currency volatility in BBVA's core growth regions, particularly Mexico and Turkey. Elevated interest rate uncertainty and foreign exchange fluctuations in these key international markets raise questions over near-term profit translation and credit quality. Though the bank continues to demonstrate solid underlying earnings power, exposure to volatile emerging market dynamics is prompting increased caution among market participants.

The decline also reflects broader sector-wide pressure across European and international financial institutions. Surging fixed-income yields and general risk aversion have induced profit-taking across top-performing bank equities that recently traded near multi-year valuation peaks. items.t: Improve Your Retirement Income with These 3 Top-Ranked Dividend Stocks
sum: Believe it or not, seniors fear running out of cash more than they fear dying.

And unfortunately, even retirees who have built a nest egg have good reason to be concerned-with the traditional approaches to retirement planning, income may no longer cover expenses. That means retirees are dipping into principal to make ends meet, setting up a race against time between dwindling investment balances and longer lifespans.
Retirement investing approaches of the past don't work today.

For example, 10-year Treasury bonds in the late 1990s offered a yield of around 6.50%, which translated to an income source you could count on. However, today's yield is much lower and probably not a viable return option to fund typical retirements.
While this yield reduction may not seem drastic, it adds up: for a $1 million investment in 10-year Treasuries, the rate drop means a difference in yield of more than $1 million.

Today's retirees are getting hit hard by reduced bond yields-and the Social Security picture isn't too rosy either. Right now and for the near future, Social Security benefits are still being paid, but it has been estimated that the Social Security funds will be depleted as soon as 2035.

How can you avoid dipping into your principal when the investments you counted on in retirement aren't producing income? You can only cut your expenses so far, and the only other option is to find a different investment vehicle to generate income.

items.t: PNC's Expansion Strategy: Growth Through Acquisitions & Partnerships
sum: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. PNC is pursuing growth with a clear strategy to expand in attractive markets, deepen customer relationships and strengthen fee-based capabilities through acquisitions and partnerships. While the banking industry continues to navigate market volatility, rising expenses and commercial real estate pressure, PNC is using inorganic growth to build scale and diversify its revenue opportunities.

A major pillar of this playbook is the acquisition of FirstBank Holding Company, completed in January 2026. The deal significantly expanded PNC's presence in Colorado and Arizona, two high-growth banking markets. FirstBank added $26.8 billion in assets and 95 branches, more than tripling PNC's branch network in Colorado. It also strengthened PNC's Arizona footprint, expanding the bank's network to more than 70 branches. In Denver, the acquisition made PNC the leading bank by retail deposit share and branch share, creating a stronger platform for commercial, corporate, private banking and retail growth. Management expects the FirstBank acquisition to be earnings accretive, adding nearly $1 per share by 2027, with integration expected to be completed by mid-June 2026.

PNC's acquisition strategy extends beyond traditional banking. In August 2025, the company acquired Aqueduct Capital Group to strengthen fund placement services at Harris Williams, its global investment banking arm. Earlier, PNC bought Linga, a point-of-sale and payment solutions firm, to expand its corporate payments capabilities in the hospitality and restaurant sectors. Its 2021 acquisition of BBVA USA also remains a defining step in building a broader national franchise.

Partnerships are other important parts of the growth formula. In 2025, PNC partnered with Coinbase, aimed at expanding access to trusted, secure and innovative digital asset solutions to PNC's banking clients and institutional investors. In 2024, PNC partnered with Plaid for secure customer data sharing and expanded its TCW Group alliance to offer private credit solutions, strengthening its presence in emerging financial services beyond branch expansion.
Overall, PNC Financial's inorganic expansion efforts support a growth strategy centered on scale, innovation and client-focused expansion.

sum: The new National Housing Plan 2026-2030 seeks to increase the scarce public housing supply in Spain. Despite tripling resources and safeguarding public ownership, its budget allocation is insufficient given the high rate of household creation.
- The construction of subsidized housing has fallen to around 13,000 units annually since 2018, which represents less than 2% of the national housing stock compared to the European average of 8%.
- With a state investment of nearly 7 billion euros, the housing stock is expected to increase by barely 33,000 units through subsidies of 85,000 euros per built home.
- The goal of mobilizing empty homes in urban centers will have a limited effect, given that most unoccupied properties are concentrated in rural areas with no imbalances between supply and demand.
- The autonomous communities will need to contribute 40% of the funds, which requires complex regional coordination for the Plan to succeed and to avoid creating inequalities.
- To attract capital and accelerate construction, it will be essential to improve legal certainty, guarantee attractive returns, and increase the availability of buildable land.

Spain | Economic cycle and housing prices
sum: Published on Thursday, April 16, 2026 | Updated on Friday, April 17, 2026

The observatory analyzes the cyclical evolution of the Spanish economy and housing prices in 2025. GDP closed the year with solid growth (2.8%), supported by domestic demand (contributed 3.6 pp to growth), while the labor market remained strong. The rise in the relative price of housing stands out in the current cycle.
- GDP per working-age person stood in Q4 2025 at 0.5 percentage points above its trend, confirming the recovery of Spain’s historical potential growth rate, at around 1% annually.

- The recent increase in housing prices reflects a combination of robust demand and insufficient supply, with a key difference from the pre-2008 cycle: the main bottleneck lies in residential capital, while credit is not acting as a factor driving housing price increases.

- Housing investment per working-age person remained below pre-pandemic levels for several years and only slightly exceeded them at the end of 2025. This reinforces the idea that a substantial part of the adjustment must come from the supply side, increasing the elasticity of the housing stock and improving the efficiency with which investment is transformed into available housing.

- Housing demand in Spain continues to be supported by relatively favorable financial fundamentals, with the ratio of housing costs to disposable income clearly more contained than in the final phase of the previous boom, and with household debt below the EU8 average.

- On the supply side, residential construction remains insufficient to absorb demand pressures, especially in a context of strong population growth. This helps explain why, compared to the slight decline in prices in the EU8 since 2022, housing prices in Spain have grown at an average annual rate of 7.5% over the last three years.

items.t: BBVA to pay €0.60 per share in cash this Friday, the second payment of a record 2025 dividend
sum: BBVA is to pay a final dividend this Friday, April 10, of €0.60 gross per share in cash. In addition to a gross payment of €0.32 per share last November, BBVA will distribute a record of €5.2 billion in ordinary dividends corresponding to the 2025 earnings, equivalent to 50 percent of the profit for the year.

The dividend that BBVA shareholders are to receive on April 10 completes the shareholder returns for the 2025 financial year, following the interim payment of €0.32 gross per share made on November 7th. Taking both payments into account, 2025 total dividend amounts to €0.92 per share, 31 percent higher than 2024 cash dividend and the highest paid by BBVA to date. In fact, the cash dividend per share has increased year after year since 2021, tripling the figures recorded at that time.

BBVA maintains a strong capital base that allows it to continue growing robustly and to sustain attractive shareholder returns, both through its ordinary policy and through its commitment to progressively distribute any excess capital above its 12% CET1 target¹.

BBVA’s shareholder ordinary remuneration policy foresees an annual payout of between 40 and 50 percent of consolidated profit and may combine cash dividends—in two payments, interim and final—with share buybacks.

In addition to the execution of this policy, BBVA has completed two extraordinary share buybacks in recent years: €3.16 billion between 2021 and 2022 and €1 billion in 2023. Furthermore, in December 2025, BBVA announced a new extraordinary buyback programme of close to €4 billion, the largest in its history, whose first tranche, of €1.5 billion, ended on March 6 and whose second tranche, of €1 billion, began on March 23².

Furthermore, including dividends and share price appreciation, since January 2019, the total value for BBVA shareholders has multiplied six-fold, well above the performance of European and Spanish banks, whose shareholders have seen their investment multiply approximately 3-fold.

items.t: Peru Economic Outlook – March 2026
sum: Published on Thursday, March 12, 2026 | Updated on Thursday, March 26, 2026

The Peruvian economy keeps showing a solid performance, supported by the dynamism of private spending. Recently, however, three negative supply shocks have affected it, driving down the output growth forecast for 2026 from 3,1 % to 2,9 %. In 2027, the supply shocks will have dissipated and GDP will grow by 3,1 %.

- The external environment remains positive for Peru. The Middle East conflict represents a new challenge for the global economy, but in the base scenario it is expected to be brief and to have a limited macroeconomic impact. In this context, terms of trade will remain at high levels, exceeding those forecasted three months ago.

- Locally, two additional supply shocks are affecting the Peruvian economy: the deterioration of weather conditions, with anomalies expected to persist for most of the year, and the domestic gas supply squeeze, relatively brief but with a sharp impact in 2026. On balance, together with external conditions, these shocks lead to a downward revision of the 2026 output growth forecast from 3,1 % to 2,9 %.

- The fiscal deficit went down in 2025, but this reduction is not expected to repeat over the next two years when higher spending on public sector wages in 2026 and purchases of military equipment are now considered. Legislative initiatives that increase public spending and the recurring losses of the state-owned oil company remain persistent risks.

- The domestic currency, which in recent weeks changed trend, weakening abruptly and sharply against the dollar amid the conflict in the Middle East, will benefit from high terms of trade and will tend again to appreciate after the general elections (2Q26). The exchange rate is expected to close this year between 3,25 and 3,35 soles per dollar.

- The negative supply shocks currently affecting the Peruvian economy are not only weakening economic activity but are also having a temporary upward impact on inflation, especially in the short term. In this environment, the Central Bank will not make changes to the monetary policy interest rate, currently at 4,25 %.

The bank will submit to the Annual General Meeting a proposal for a final dividend of €0.60 per share, in addition to the €0.32 per share paid in November. In total, €0.92 per share in cash—the highest dividend in the bank’s history. In addition, an extraordinary share buyback program of nearly €4 billion was announced last December.

Beyond its financial results, BBVA has strengthened its role as a driver of social progress. In 2025, the bank supported more than 160,000 families in purchasing their homes and backed one million SMEs and self-employed individuals in growing their businesses, as well as 73,000 larger companies.

The year also marked the first year of the new Strategic Plan, with significant progress in priority segments such as corporate banking and sustainable business. During the year, BBVA channeled €134 billion in sustainable finance, a record figure that brings the Group closer to its target of reaching €700 billion in sustainable finance by 2029. In addition, it added 11.5 million new customers and closed the year as one of the most recommended banks in its core markets.

BBVA has radically embedded the customer perspective into everything it does. The bank has evolved from “thinking about the customer” to “thinking like the customer,” with the aim of delivering excellence in every interaction.

In 2025, BBVA also took a decisive step to lead the era of artificial intelligence, always at the service of people. Key initiatives include Blue, the assistant integrated into the bank’s app, and the strategic partnership with OpenAI.
None of these achievements would have been possible without the more than 127,000 people who are part of the Group.

items.t: BBVA is strongest banking brand in Mexico | Press Release
sum: New data from Brand Finance reveals strongest banking brands among Mexican customers

LONDON, 4 March 2026 – BBVA is the strongest banking brand among Mexican customers, according to new data from Brand Finance, the world’s leading brand valuation consultancy. Brand Finance data reveals that BBVA leads on brand strength metrics in Mexico, reflecting strong performance across consideration, preference, and likeability. According to the bank, its long-term strategy includes plans to invest more than 100 billion pesos by 2030 to support improvements in key areas, including customer experience.

Mexico-native Banamex ranks second among Mexico’s strongest banking brands and records the highest Brand Strength Index (BSI) score among domestic peers, driven by improved customer consideration, preference, and recommendation scores, according to Brand Finance research. Santander ranks third in Mexico for its brand strength.

In terms of brand value, four Mexican banking brands feature in the Banking 500 2026 ranking. Banorte remains the country’s most valuable banking brand at USD2.6 billion, up 7% from 2025. Inbursa records the largest brand value increase among Mexican brands, rising 78% to USD659.8 million. Banco Azteca and Compartamos Banco also ranking among the world’s most valuable banking brands.
Laurence Newell, Executive Chairman, Americas, Brand Finance commented:

“Mexico’s banking sector continues to demonstrate strong brand momentum across both domestic and international players. BBVA’s leadership on brand strength reflects sustained investment customer experience in this market, while Banorte’s position as the country’s most valuable banking brand highlights the scale and resilience of leading domestic institutions, underscoring the growing competitiveness of the market.”
The total brand value of the world’s 500 most valuable and strongest banking brands increased 10% in 2026 to USD1.8 trillion, marking five years of continued growth.

items.t: Earnings: BBVA Posts Record Profit of €10.5 Billion in 2025 and Will Distribute a Dividend of More Than €5.2 Billion
sum: BBVA reported a profit of €10.5 billion in 2025 (+4.5 percent yoy), the highest in its history, mostly driven by core revenues. The BBVA Group stood out for its unique combination of growth and profitability, leading in Europe: lending increased by 16.2 percent (in constant euros) while ROTE reached 19.3 percent. Furthermore, BBVA maintained a solid CET1 capital ratio of 12.7 percent and continued to drive value creation for shareholders, with a tangible book value per share plus dividends growing 15.2 percent¹. In addition, the bank is set to distribute a dividend of €0.92 per share² in cash, the highest ever. This amounts to a total of €5.25 billion³, representing a cash dividend 31 percent higher than that of 2024. Combined with the nearly €4 billion share buyback program announced in December, this represents more than €9.2 billion.

“2025 was another excellent year for BBVA. We earned a record-breaking profit and once again, we stood out for our unique combination of growth and profitability. This outstanding performance has resulted in an excellent value creation, which allows us to significantly accelerate shareholder remuneration, with a record dividend and the largest share buyback program to date,” BBVA Chair Carlos Torres Vila said. “We look to 2026 with positive prospects in all our markets and we expect to continue growing faster than our peers and increase profitability to levels around 20 percent. BBVA is at its best moment. The new Strategic Plan provides a very clear roadmap and the bank is well positioned to deliver on the ambitious targets through 2028,” he added.

BBVA’s earnings in 2025 were driven by momentum in banking activity and customer growth. Lending increased by 16.2 percent in constant euros, supported by gains in market share in the Group’s main markets (+20 bps in Spain, +29 in Mexico and +36 in Türkiye). This growth had a positive impact on society: in 2025, 160,000 families purchased a home; one million SMEs and self-employed workers boosted their business with new loans, and 73,000 larger companies invested in their growth. Moreover, BBVA channeled €30.2 billion in social initiatives, such as the construction of hospitals and schools.

Garanti BBVA Shows Solid Performance, Reports Robust 2025 Earnings
sum: Garanti BBVA announced its financial results for 2025, reporting a net income of TL 111.26 billion. Total assets reached TL 4.55 trillion, and lending stood at TL 3.49 trillion. Customer deposits amounted to TL 3.14 trillion, representing growth of 50 percent over the previous year. Meanwhile, the bank maintained its strong capital position, with a capital adequacy ratio of 17.5¹ percent. Return on average equity (ROAE) reached 29.1 percent and return on average assets (ROAA) was 2.9 percent.

Garanti BBVA’s CEO Mahmut Akten noted that the gradual normalization process, shaped by disinflation targets in both global and domestic monetary policy, required a disciplined and strategic response from the banking sector throughout the year. He emphasized that policymakers’ resolute stance led to notable progress in inflation, with monetary policy implemented within a controlled framework.

The banking sector felt the effects of this economic rebalancing. Deposit costs remained above the policy rate due to regulations around Turkish lira deposits, and therefore became a key factor in balance sheet management. Loan growth was contained within the limits set by regulations.

Garanti BBVA once again demonstrated its strong management capabilities and balance sheet strength, sustaining its robust performance throughout the year. The CEO pointed to the bank’s figures from the year, with total assets reaching TL 4.5 trillion and a TL loan portfolio of TL 1.7 trillion.

The bank strengthened its long-standing leadership in TL lending, gaining market share and preserving a balanced composition of retail and corporate loans. Garanti BBVA’s clear leadership in retail lending was reinforced by market share gains across all product categories. The bank also maintained its position as the leading private bank in total cash and non-cash corporate loans.

Payment systems continued to distinguish the bank from its competitors and remained a key source of long-term value creation. On the funding side, a customer-based and well-diversified funding structure supported sustainable balance sheet management. Total customer deposits exceeded TL 3 trillion, while funding sources were further diversified.
